title: Missense variants
summary: Single amino-acid changes in a human protein: predicted effect, frequency in people, clinical classification, and the protein's predicted fold.

concepts.label: Protein
concepts.description: A human protein (UniProt accession, set with the uniprot parameter) and its gene (gene parameter); the two must name the same protein.

children.label: Residue
children.description: One amino acid of the chain, numbered from the N-terminus.

children.label: pLDDT
children.description: AlphaFold's per-residue confidence, 0–100. Below 50 usually means intrinsically disordered: no fixed position to predict.

children.label: Missense variant
children.description: A DNA change that swaps one amino acid for another (e.g. R175H). Only some of the 19 alternatives at a residue are one DNA letter away.

children.label: AlphaMissense pathogenicity
children.description: Google DeepMind's predicted probability that the change is pathogenic (Cheng et al. 2023); ≥ 0.564 likely pathogenic, ≤ 0.34 likely benign. Trained on population frequencies and structure context, not on ClinVar labels.

children.label: Allele frequency
children.description: The share of chromosomes carrying the change in gnomAD v4 (exomes and genomes, about 807,000 people).

children.label: Clinical significance
children.description: ClinVar's classification (pathogenic, benign, uncertain, conflicting), with its review stars.
